entry_conditions: Observed support for normal entry is the home arm posture with both gripper fingers open near 0.04 m, drawer_position near 0 m, and the red block on the drawer-front region around x 0.093-0.108 m, y -0.077 to -0.055 m, z 0.063 m. The model can also be invoked partway through the learned transition when the causal state shows a consistent side-grasp pull state: TCP low near the red/drawer front, finger aperture indicating open/closing/closed status, drawer_position and drawer_velocity indicating progress, and red pose approximately co-moving with the drawer along world x.
exit_conditions: A useful exit state for the successor has drawer_position greater than about 0.26 m, the red block still at the open drawer front near z 0.063 m, gripper fingers reopened near 0.04 m each, and the TCP retreating upward/away from the low side-grasp pose. In the demonstrations this corresponds to the post-release part of the overlap, with drawer_position approximately 0.30 m and TCP height increasing from about 0.13 m toward 0.37 m.
overlap_role: The [240,330) overlap is included in this model, so it learns the release, drawer-open confirmation, and upward/away retreat that prepare the scene for red_top_regrasp_lift. The overlap is not treated as a hard switch point; the inference agent can continue this policy while the causal observation still indicates release/retreat is in progress, or transfer once the successor has a clear open-finger, open-drawer, above/front-of-red state.
successor_readiness: red_top_regrasp_lift should receive an open drawer, red still visible and stationary on the drawer front surface rather than already carried, open gripper fingers, and a TCP pose with enough clearance to descend from above. Causal cues are drawer_position above about 0.26 m, low drawer_velocity, finger width near 0.08 m total, red z near 0.063 m, and TCP no longer squeezing the side of the red block.
failure_signatures: Possible failures include drawer_position remaining below about 0.26 m after the pull phase, red not translating with the drawer/TCP during the closed-finger pull, fingers not closing near the side-grasp contact or not reopening before retreat, TCP remaining jammed low at the drawer face, or red pose changing in a way inconsistent with the measured side-pull demonstrations. These are observation cues for the inference agent, not implemented recovery controllers.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy from approach through side grasp while drawer_position is small and the TCP-red geometry is converging to the side-grasp relation. Continue during the pull while fingers are closed and drawer_position is increasing. Continue after the drawer opens if fingers are still closed or the TCP is still low, because the expanded slice teaches release and retreat. Consider transferring after the gripper is open, drawer is open, red remains on the drawer surface, and TCP has retreated upward/away enough for an overhead regrasp.
limitations: The handoff conditions describe measured support and inferred contact readiness; they are not hard geometric guarantees. This policy uses only the state vector, contains no IK, no vision, and no scripted fallback. It is untested for large initial red variations, drawer friction changes, missed first pinches, or red rotations/slips outside the twelve demonstrations.
